tests/gold/review.c::gcc-O1::sext.cause: `movsbw %dil,%ax` writes only AX and keeps RAX's upper bytes; `lea 0x0(,%rax,4),%edx; sub %edx,%eax` then computes EAX, whose bits 16..31 come from RAX's entry value. The source returns int16_t, so no caller reads them, but the recovered result is uint32_t, which demands them: the read is a residual held from entry. A written-lane result width (AX) would leave them undemanded. Before, this record carried gate_three's setcc cause (audit T20).

Both returns render `return r2sleigh_residual_u64(n)` and the FP accumulation is elided as unobserved.
